name: GP Brunswick Cellulose Mill - Brunswick GA

fieldNotes.truckGate: Large bleached-kraft pulp mill receiving ~1,000 truckloads of pine logs per day; single controlled access road off the city street network; container/trailer yard is fenced with chain-link and privacy screening (Street View, Nov 2024).
fieldNotes.guardShack: No frontal booth view obtained (no Street View on the private mill road), but a 600-employee pulp mill handling ~1,000 trucks/day operates a staffed gatehouse by standard. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.scale: Pulp mills weigh inbound wood loads on truck scales; inferred true for a mill receiving 1,000 truckloads/day. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Very large container/trailer drop yard NE of the process buildings - hundreds of intermodal containers on chassis (UASC, Hapag-Lloyd visible in Street View) plus trailers; clearly 50+.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Bleached-kraft mill ships baled/containerized fluff pulp; finished-goods dock banks are limited - 10-25 band, ~20 estimated. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: Active rail yard with rail cars along the NW edge of the woodyard; rail serves the mill.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Extensive paved width at the container-yard entrance allows an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Large multi-building campus: kraft process buildings, recovery, woodyard, baleline, container yard, plus extensive settling-pond/clarifier complex.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Mill is on the Turtle River at the edge of Brunswick, bordered by residential neighborhoods and a cemetery, but the broader setting is a small coastal city / edge-of-town - judged Rural per rubric (small-town industrial).
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Ample paved approach from the access road to the container yard provides deep truck queuing.
fieldNotes.perimeter: Box covers the developed footprint - process buildings, woodyard, and the NE container/trailer drop yard; excludes outlying settling ponds and sludge fields.
